works.title: Ship at Kasimedu
works.story: Before dawn one morning in 1997, a student at the art college took the 22A bus from Thiruvanmiyur, bound for Tiruvottiyur at the far end of the city, to make outdoor studies at Kasimedu, the fishing harbour of north Chennai. The bus went on, and on, and on; at last he got off and made a few ink-wash sketches of the boats hauled up on the shore. This painting was made from those sketches. It was one of the works he had set aside never to sell, and it is the one that got away: shown with the Square Group at Saga Art Gallery that year, it was acquired by Mdm Monika, his head of art history.
works.exhibitions: Square Group: Paintings and Sculptures, Saga Art Gallery, Chennai, 15–30 September 1997

works.title: Self-portrait
works.medium: Orange pastel and conté on paper
works.story: Made on 13 April 2020, two weeks after a long-bearded self-portrait, this drawing set the language baaskaraa has worked in since. The head and beard are built inside a cubic scaffold of construction lines, and one unbroken line moves through it, gathering at points that radiate like stars. The idea came from his own long beard: if a single hair can flow into a shape with volume, a single continuous line can make a form. He saw the same truth in the banyan, whose hanging roots begin as fine as hair and grow until they shape the tree.
works.signature: Signed baaskaraa and dated 13420 8P (13 April 2020, 8 PM)

projects.partners: Maya Dance Theatre (presenter) · Apsara Asia Pte Ltd (project management, marketing) · Singai Tamil Sangam (venue) · Kampong Glam Rowell Court Residents' Committee and Republic Polytechnic Indian Cultural Group (community painting) · Supporters on the promo card: Apsara Asia, Nippon Paint, Lee Foundation, Singai Tamil Sangam, arts fund, OCBC Bank
projects.role: Visuals and murals, with Charlie Lim (credited in the programme as 'Ka Baskar'); promotional video made by Baskar in support of the event
projects.summary: GREY was a Maya Dance Theatre production staged on the rooftop of Singai Tamil Sangam, 02 Kampong Kapor Road, Little India, from 19 to 22 June 2013 at 8 pm. The programme credits the visuals and murals to Charlie Lim and Ka. Baskar: the rooftop walls, stairhouse and parapets were painted as a mural that became the environment for the dance, with members of the Kampong Glam Rowell Court Residents' Committee and students from the Republic Polytechnic Indian Cultural Group painting alongside. Baskar also made a promotional video in support of the event.

projects.title: Project LAVA: Bird Sanctum
projects.subtitle: A Tamil novel turned into an installation for the NAC–NLB Project LAVA in the Libraries
projects.partners: National Arts Council (NAC) · National Library Board (NLB)
projects.role: Appointed LAVA artist (Tamil): proposal, design, making, installation at four libraries, public talk
projects.summary: Bird Sanctum was one of four artworks chosen for the second Project LAVA in the Libraries, the NAC and NLB programme that pairs Singapore writing with visual art. It turned Ma Ilangkannan's Tamil novel Kuruvi Kottam into an installation of white birds around a nest that stands for home, on a pedestal in the shape of Singapore, and it travelled to four public libraries from May to August 2014.
